en: Itivuttaka 37 Dukanipāta, Paṭhamavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then the venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side. As he was sitting there, the venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “‘The mind, the mind,’ it is said, Blessed One. To what extent, Blessed One, is ‘mind’ said? “Ānanda, when the eye arises, it is called ‘mind’; when the ear arises, it is called ‘mind’; when the nose arises, it is called ‘mind’; when the tongue arises, it is called ‘mind’; when the body arises, it is called ‘mind’; when the mind arises, it is called ‘mind. Ānanda, when the eye ceases, it is called ‘mind’; when the ear ceases, it is called ‘mind’; when the nose ceases, it is called ‘mind’; when the tongue ceases, it is called ‘mind’; when the body ceases, it is called ‘mind’; when the mind ceases, it is called ‘mind. “It is wonderful, Blessed One! It is marvelous, Blessed One! How well this has been stated by the Blessed One: ‘Ānanda, when the eye arises, it is called “mind”; when the ear arises... when the mind arises, it is called “mind. Ānanda, when the eye ceases, it is called “mind”; when the ear ceases... when the mind ceases, it is called “mind. Blessed One, I understand this thus: ‘When the eye arises, it is called “mind”; when the ear arises... when the mind arises, it is called “mind. When the eye ceases, it is called “mind”; when the ear ceases... when the mind ceases, it is called “mind. “Good, good, Ānanda! It is well that you understand this thus: ‘When the eye arises, it is called “mind”; when the ear arises... when the mind arises, it is called “mind. When the eye ceases, it is called “mind”; when the ear ceases... when the mind ceases, it is called “mind. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, the venerable Ānanda rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world.

What two? The person who is a trainee and the person who is one beyond training. These are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. The Somanassa Sutta.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, possessed of two qualities, a bhikkhu dwells abundant in happiness and joy even in this very life, and the basis for the destruction of the taints is undertaken by him."
"Which two?
Arousing a sense of urgency regarding things that should arouse urgency, and, being thus stirred, applying oneself with wise effort.
Endowed with these two qualities, monks, a bhikkhu dwells abundant in happiness and joy in this very life, and he has set forth for the destruction of the taints."
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
“In places that inspire a sense of urgency,…”
The wise person should indeed be stirred;
the bhikkhu, ardent and discerning,
should examine with wisdom.
Dwelling thus, ardent,
of peaceful conduct and unagitated,
devoted to mental tranquility,
“May one reach the destruction of suffering.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The tenth [sutta].
The First Chapter.
Its summary:
Two monks, and those things that cause remorse.
The "to be heated" [factors] are ten by way of others;
the "ardent" and the "non-deceptive" are two;
with "joy," they are ten.
